articles.full_text:
15th October 2026 - Link Blog Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue up nearly 50% to $16.8bn ahead of IPO .

The phrase "told investors" appears four times in this FT article, which reports on Anthropic's day of hosting investors on Wednesday.

Lots of details in here from " people with knowledge of the matter ".

Key things I learned from the article: Q1 revenue (Jan/Feb/Mar) was "about $4.8bn" Q2 (Apr/May/Jun) was $11.5bn Q3 (Jul/Aug/Sep) was $16.8bn In Q3: $1.70 in revenue for every $1 spent on "computing power" Adjusted operating margins (excluding stock-based compensation) were 11% This point about distillation is worth quoting in full (highlight mine): The start-up has also clamped down on “distillation” — a controversial practice whereby rival AI labs train their models on the outputs of more advanced ones.

When rival companies “distil” their models from Anthropic’s models, that involves heavy usage and spending.

Anthropic told investors on Wednesday distillation accounted for 5 per cent to 7 per cent of revenue and that they had cut it back “materially” in the third quarter of the year, said four people with direct knowledge of the matter.

Napkin maths says that if distillation was 5% of their Q2 revenue (before they cut it back in Q3) then unnamed "other labs" spent over half a billion dollars distilling Anthropic's models in that quarter!

Also notable: Anthropic appear to no longer be leaning on "annualized run-rate revenue" ( previously ) in these communications to their investors.

articles.full_text:
AI News Tech ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now With the ChatGPT extension installed, it can pull information from your open tabs or bring the AI bot into the sidebar.﻿ With the ChatGPT extension installed, it can pull information from your open tabs or bring the AI bot into the sidebar.﻿ by Stevie Bonifield Oct 15, 2026, 10:43 PM UTC Link Share Gift Image: OpenAI Stevie Bonifield is a news writer covering all things consumer tech.

Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

OpenAI’s ChatGPT Atlas browser is gone , but now ChatGPT’s Google Chrome extension is getting some upgrades that allow it to use the browser tabs you already have open.

With the extension installed, OpenAI says ChatGPT can now view your browser tabs when you tag Chrome in ChatGPT’s web or desktop app, posting a demo video showing someone asking ChatGPT to compare the three tabs they have open with sofas they’re considering.

Here are some of the sample queries OpenAI listed for using the upgraded add-on: Use the details in this event brief to fill out the registration form, and stop before submitting.

Put the vendors in these tabs into my comparison sheet, with pricing, key features, and source links.

Look at all the tabs I have open and compare the contractor services.

Then draft an email to the one that fits my home renovation.

Fill out the form I have open in @chrome ahead of seeing my new dentist.

Also, can you add the appointment to my work and personal calendar.

It’s also updated ChatGPT in the sidebar , with “the full power of ChatGPT” and your entire conversation history in Chat or Work to use without leaving the page you’re viewing.

It also enables ChatGPT Work to “control” your Chrome tabs for tasks like “sending messages, filling out forms, or downloading files,” similar to Google’s Gemini-powered “auto browse” feature , as well as organize or group open tabs.

Tech AI News Bluesky’s AI tool now lets you make games and apps to share on social Attie launched earlier this year as a way to build your own feeds with AI, but Bluesky is expanding what it can do.﻿ Attie launched earlier this year as a way to build your own feeds with AI, but Bluesky is expanding what it can do.﻿ by Jay Peters Oct 15, 2026, 7:57 PM UTC Link Share Gift Image: Bluesky Jay Peters is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more.

He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.

Bluesky’s Attie AI tool, which initially launched earlier this year as a way to use AI to build your own feeds, now lets you make “small” social apps like games, polls, and dashboards that you can then share with others as their own websites.

In an interview at TechCrunch Disrupt , Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider said to think of Attie as “social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community.” You can make your own Attie app by typing in a prompt.

A simple poll I made about Pokémon Red and Pokémon Blue took a few minutes to generate.

If you want to check out something more full-featured, the Attie website currently highlights a few examples like a “Flappy Butterfly” Flappy Bird clone , a drum machine , a quiz , and an idle clicker about a celery man , and each has a custom link on the attie.site domain and attribution for who made the social app at the bottom of the page.

The apps I’ve messed around with are pretty lightweight novelties, though I liked the drum machine.

articles.title: Anthropic is letting METR researchers look under the hood with employee-level access
articles.summary: METR will publish its own assessments of Anthropic’s risks, incidents, and practices, and the frontier AI model maker has given up the right to block them.
articles.full_text:
Anthropic is giving employee-level access to six researchers from METR , a nonprofit that tests frontier AI models, to independently assess Anthropic’s models, safety practices, and risk management, the company said in a blog post on Thursday.

The arrangement comes at a time where incidents of AI agents acting outside their instructions have been disclosed every week or two since late August.

The incidents have sharpened calls for independent checks on AI companies. “We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making,” Anthropic said in the blog post. “We aim to close the gap between what evaluators understand about a frontier AI company’s systems and what the company itself understands.” Under the new arrangement, the METR team has Anthropic-issued company laptops, office space, and access to internal tools roughly on par with what Anthropic’s own risk assessment teams use. “Anthropic employees are encouraged to share information with them just as they would with a fellow employee working on alignment risk” the company said.

Anthropic compared the arrangement to banking, similar to how regulators place resident examiners inside the largest banks.  METR will publish its own assessments of Anthropic’s risks, incidents, and practices, and the company has given up the right to block them. “Anthropic can’t veto publication, but we can require them to redact information if it falls into narrow, pre-defined categories,” the company said, such as customer data, anything attorney-client privileged, or relating to information about its model architectures. “METR is free to characterize our redactions publicly, and say whether it believes the redactions were justified, as long as it does so without revealing the redacted information” Anthropic added.

METR is the only evaluator so far at the top of a three-tier system Anthropic is building.

Evaluators in the bottom tier, like biosecurity nonprofit SecureBio, run narrow reviews and require Anthropic’s approval to publish.

The middle tier gets more information and can publish without approval, while the top tier adds METR’s employee-level access.  Thursday’s announcement makes good on a promise Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei made in a September essay , where he proposed embedding outside evaluators inside AI labs as a first step toward slowing the technology’s development.

OpenAI quickly pledged the same , and both companies, along with Google, Meta, Nvidia, and xAI, have since signed a White House accord committing to independent review.
